schema.manifest_field: type: string required: true default: (none — only required field if manifest is present) applicability: cli excerpt: | Unique identifier (kebab-case, no spaces). This name is used for namespacing components. For example, in the UI, the agent `agent-creator` for the plugin with name `plugin-dev` will appear as `plugin-dev:agent-creator`. caveats: - "The manifest itself is optional. If omitted, Claude Code auto-discovers components in default locations and derives the plugin name from the directory name." - "If you include a manifest, `name` is the only required field." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / Required fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: (none) applicability: cli excerpt: | Semantic version. If also set in the marketplace entry, `plugin.json` takes priority. You only need to set it in one place. caveats: - "Claude Code uses the version to determine whether to update your plugin. If you change your plugin's code but don't bump the version in `plugin.json`, your plugin's existing users won't see your changes due to caching." - "If your plugin is within a marketplace directory, you can manage the version through `marketplace.json` instead and omit the `version` field from `plugin.json`." - "Version format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (semantic versioning)." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / Metadata fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

type: string|array|object required: false default: "monitors/monitors.json" applicability: cli excerpt: | Background Monitor configurations that auto-arm when the plugin is enabled at session start or when a skill in this plugin is invoked. Example: `"./monitors.json"` caveats: - "A custom path replaces the default. If the manifest specifies `monitors`, the default `monitors/monitors.json` is not loaded." - "All paths must be relative to the plugin root and start with `./`" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / Component path fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

type: object required: false default: (none) applicability: cli excerpt: | User-configurable values prompted at enable time. Use this instead of requiring users to hand-edit `settings.json`.
Keys must be valid identifiers. Each value is available for substitution as `${user_config.KEY}` in MCP and LSP server configs, hook commands, and (for non-sensitive values only) skill and agent content. Values are also exported to plugin subprocesses as `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` environment variables.
Non-sensitive values are stored in `settings.json` under `pluginConfigs[<plugin-id>].options`. Sensitive values go to the system keychain (or `~/.claude/.credentials.json` where the keychain is unavailable). Keychain storage is shared with OAuth tokens and has an approximately 2 KB total limit, so keep sensitive values small. caveats: - "Each key maps to an object with `description` (string) and `sensitive` (boolean)." - "Sensitive values are NOT available in skill/agent content — only in MCP/LSP configs and hook commands." - "Keychain has ~2 KB total limit; keep sensitive values small." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / User configuration" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

type: array required: false default: (none) applicability: cli excerpt: | Channel declarations for message injection (Telegram, Slack, Discord style). Each channel binds to an MCP server that the plugin provides.
The `server` field is required and must match a key in the plugin's `mcpServers`. The optional per-channel `userConfig` uses the same schema as the top-level field, letting the plugin prompt for bot tokens or owner IDs when the plugin is enabled. caveats: - "Each channel object requires a `server` field matching a key in `mcpServers`." - "Per-channel `userConfig` is optional and uses the same schema as top-level `userConfig`." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / Channels" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

type: array required: false default: (none) applicability: cli excerpt: | Other plugins this plugin requires, optionally with semver version constraints. Example: `[{ "name": "secrets-vault", "version": "~2.1.0" }]` caveats: - "Each entry is either a string (plugin name) or an object with `name` and optional `version` (semver constraint)." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / Component path fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00
schema.component_type: default_location: "skills/" alternate_location: "commands/" file_format: | Skills are directories with `SKILL.md`. Commands are simple flat markdown files. Skill structure: skills/ ├── pdf-processor/ │ ├── SKILL.md │ ├── reference.md (optional) │ └── scripts/ (optional) └── code-reviewer/ └── SKILL.md integration_behavior: | * Skills and commands are automatically discovered when the plugin is installed * Claude can invoke them automatically based on task context * Skills can include supporting files alongside SKILL.md caveats: - "Use `skills/` for new plugins; `commands/` is a legacy flat-file format." - "The `commands/` directory contains flat `.md` files; `skills/` uses subdirectory-per-skill with `SKILL.md`." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin components reference / Skills" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

default_location: "agents/" file_format: "Markdown files with YAML frontmatter describing agent capabilities." frontmatter_fields_supported: "name, description, model, effort, maxTurns, tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, isolation" frontmatter_fields_excluded: "hooks, mcpServers, permissionMode (not supported for plugin-shipped agents for security reasons)" isolation_valid_values: '"worktree" (only valid value)' frontmatter_example: | --- name: agent-name description: What this agent specializes in and when Claude should invoke it model: sonnet effort: medium maxTurns: 20 disallowedTools: Write, Edit ---
Detailed system prompt for the agent describing its role, expertise, and behavior. integration_behavior: | * Agents appear in the `/agents` interface * Claude can invoke agents automatically based on task context * Agents can be invoked manually by users * Plugin agents work alongside built-in Claude agents source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin components reference / Agents" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

default_location: "hooks/hooks.json" alternate_locations: "inline in plugin.json under `hooks` key" file_format: "JSON configuration with event matchers and actions." hook_types: - name: "command" description: "execute shell commands or scripts" - name: "http" description: "send the event JSON as a POST request to a URL" - name: "prompt" description: "evaluate a prompt with an LLM (uses `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder for context)" - name: "agent" description: "run an agentic verifier with tools for complex verification tasks" supported_events: | SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Notification, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, Stop, StopFailure, TeammateIdle, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, PreCompact, PostCompact, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, SessionEnd event_details: - event: "PermissionDenied" note: "Return `{retry: true}` to tell the model it may retry the denied tool call." - event: "FileChanged" note: "The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch." - event: "WorktreeCreate" note: "Replaces default git behavior." hook_config_example: | { "hooks": { "PostToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Write|Edit", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/format-code.sh" } ] } ] } } caveats: - "Hooks respond to the same lifecycle events as user-defined hooks." - "Event names are case-sensitive: `PostToolUse` not `postToolUse`." - "Hook scripts must be executable (`chmod +x`)." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin components reference / Hooks" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

manifest_key: "mcpServers" default_location: ".mcp.json" alternate_locations: "inline in plugin.json under `mcpServers` key" file_format: "Standard MCP server configuration (JSON)." config_fields: - name: "command" description: "The MCP server binary or executable to run." required: true - name: "args" description: "Command-line arguments for the server." required: false - name: "env" description: "Environment variables to set when starting the server." required: false - name: "cwd" description: "Working directory for the server process." required: false config_example: | { "mcpServers": { "plugin-database": { "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/servers/db-server", "args": ["--config", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/config.json"], "env": { "DB_PATH": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/data" } } } } integration_behavior: | * Plugin MCP servers start automatically when the plugin is enabled * Servers appear as standard MCP tools in Claude's toolkit * Server capabilities integrate seamlessly with Claude's existing tools * Plugin servers can be configured independently of user MCP servers source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin components reference / MCP servers" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

manifest_key: "lspServers" default_location: ".lsp.json" alternate_locations: "inline in plugin.json under `lspServers` key" file_format: "JSON configuration mapping language server names to their configs." required_fields: - name: "command" description: "The LSP binary to execute (must be in PATH)" - name: "extensionToLanguage" description: "Maps file extensions to language identifiers" optional_fields: - name: "args" description: "Command-line arguments for the LSP server" - name: "transport" description: "Communication transport: `stdio` (default) or `socket`" default: "stdio" - name: "env" description: "Environment variables to set when starting the server" - name: "initializationOptions" description: "Options passed to the server during initialization" - name: "settings" description: "Settings passed via `workspace/didChangeConfiguration`" - name: "workspaceFolder" description: "Workspace folder path for the server" - name: "startupTimeout" description: "Max time to wait for server startup (milliseconds)" - name: "shutdownTimeout" description: "Max time to wait for graceful shutdown (milliseconds)" - name: "restartOnCrash" description: "Whether to automatically restart the server if it crashes" - name: "maxRestarts" description: "Maximum number of restart attempts before giving up" lsp_capabilities: | * Instant diagnostics: Claude sees errors and warnings immediately after each edit * Code navigation: go to definition, find references, and hover information * Language awareness: type information and documentation for code symbols config_example: | { "go": { "command": "gopls", "args": ["serve"], "extensionToLanguage": { ".go": "go" } } } caveats: - "You must install the language server binary separately. LSP plugins configure how Claude Code connects to a language server, but they don't include the server itself." - "If you see `Executable not found in $PATH`, install the required binary." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin components reference / LSP servers" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00
schema.scope_spec:
description: | When you install a plugin, you choose a scope that determines where the plugin is available and who else can use it. Plugins use the same scope system as other Claude Code configurations.
Resolution priority (higher overrides lower): enterprise/managed > user > project > local scopes: - name: "user" settings_file: "~/.claude/settings.json" use_case: "Personal plugins available across all projects (default)" default: true - name: "project" settings_file: ".claude/settings.json" use_case: "Team plugins shared via version control" - name: "local" settings_file: ".claude/settings.local.json" use_case: "Project-specific plugins, gitignored" - name: "managed" settings_file: "(Managed settings — read-only, update only)" use_case: "Managed plugins pushed by administrators; read-only" caveats: - "The `managed` scope is read-only; plugins there can be updated but not disabled by the user." - "`--scope project` writes to `enabledPlugins` in .claude/settings.json, making the plugin available to everyone who clones the repository." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin installation scopes" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00
schema.path_rules:
general_rules: | * All paths must be relative to the plugin root and start with `./` * Components from custom paths use the same naming and namespacing rules * Multiple paths can be specified as arrays
replace_vs_additive: | For `skills`, `commands`, `agents`, `outputStyles`, and `monitors`, a custom path REPLACES the default. If the manifest specifies `skills`, the default `skills/` directory is not scanned; if it specifies `monitors`, the default `monitors/monitors.json` is not loaded.
`hooks`, `mcpServers`, and `lspServers` have DIFFERENT semantics — their handling of multiple sources does not simply replace the default.
keep_default_pattern: | To keep the default directory and add more paths for skills, commands, agents, or output styles, include the default in your array: `"skills": ["./skills/", "./extras/"]`
skill_name_resolution: | When a skill path points to a directory that contains a `SKILL.md` directly, for example `"skills": ["./"]` pointing to the plugin root, the frontmatter `name` field in `SKILL.md` determines the skill's invocation name. This gives a stable name regardless of the install directory. If `name` is not set in the frontmatter, the directory basename is used as a fallback.
environment_variables: - name: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" description: | The absolute path to your plugin's installation directory. Use this to reference scripts, binaries, and config files bundled with the plugin. This path changes when the plugin updates, so files you write here do not survive an update. available_in: "skill content, agent content, hook commands, MCP/LSP server configs, hook process env, MCP/LSP subprocess env" - name: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}" description: | A persistent directory for plugin state that survives updates. Use this for installed dependencies such as `node_modules` or Python virtual environments, generated code, caches, and any other files that should persist across plugin versions. The directory is created automatically the first time this variable is referenced. resolves_to: "~/.claude/plugins/data/{id}/ where characters outside a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _, - are replaced by -" available_in: "skill content, agent content, hook commands, MCP/LSP server configs, hook process env, MCP/LSP subprocess env" caveats: - "Deleted automatically when you uninstall the plugin from the last scope." - "Pass `--keep-data` to `plugin uninstall` to preserve it." - "Directory existence alone cannot detect when an update changes the plugin's dependency manifest — compare the bundled manifest against the copy in the data directory and reinstall when they differ."
path_traversal_limitations: | Installed plugins cannot reference files outside their directory. Paths that traverse outside the plugin root (such as `../shared-utils`) will not work after installation because those external files are not copied to the cache.
symlink_workaround: | If your plugin needs to access files outside its directory, you can create symbolic links to external files within your plugin directory. Symlinks are preserved in the cache rather than dereferenced, and they resolve to their target at runtime.
caching_behavior: | For security and verification purposes, Claude Code copies marketplace plugins to the user's local plugin cache (`~/.claude/plugins/cache`) rather than using them in-place. Each installed version is a separate directory in the cache. When you update or uninstall a plugin, the previous version directory is marked as orphaned and removed automatically 7 days later.
Plugins specified via `claude --plugin-dir` are NOT cached — they are used in-place for the duration of that session only.
source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "Plugin manifest schema / Path behavior rules" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00
schema.cli_command:
synopsis: "claude plugin install <plugin> [options]" description: "Install a plugin from available marketplaces." arguments: - name: "<plugin>" description: "Plugin name or `plugin-name@marketplace-name` for a specific marketplace" required: true options: - flags: "-s, --scope <scope>" description: "Installation scope: `user`, `project`, or `local`" default: "user" valid_values: "user, project, local" - flags: "-h, --help" description: "Display help for command" behavior: | Scope determines which settings file the installed plugin is added to. For example, `--scope project` writes to `enabledPlugins` in .claude/settings.json, making the plugin available to everyone who clones the project repository. examples: | # Install to user scope (default) claude plugin install formatter@my-marketplace
# Install to project scope (shared with team) claude plugin install formatter@my-marketplace --scope project
# Install to local scope (gitignored) claude plugin install formatter@my-marketplace --scope local source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "CLI commands reference / plugin install" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

synopsis: "claude plugin uninstall <plugin> [options]" aliases: "remove, rm" description: "Remove an installed plugin." arguments: - name: "<plugin>" description: "Plugin name or `plugin-name@marketplace-name`" required: true options: - flags: "-s, --scope <scope>" description: "Uninstall from scope: `user`, `project`, or `local`" default: "user" valid_values: "user, project, local" - flags: "--keep-data" description: "Preserve the plugin's persistent data directory" default: "(off — data is deleted by default on last-scope uninstall)" - flags: "-h, --help" description: "Display help for command" behavior: | By default, uninstalling from the last remaining scope also deletes the plugin's `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` directory. Use `--keep-data` to preserve it, for example when reinstalling after testing a new version. source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "CLI commands reference / plugin uninstall" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

synopsis: "claude plugin enable <plugin> [options]" description: "Enable a disabled plugin." arguments: - name: "<plugin>" description: "Plugin name or `plugin-name@marketplace-name`" required: true options: - flags: "-s, --scope <scope>" description: "Scope to enable: `user`, `project`, or `local`" default: "user" valid_values: "user, project, local" - flags: "-h, --help" description: "Display help for command" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "CLI commands reference / plugin enable" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

synopsis: "claude plugin disable <plugin> [options]" description: "Disable a plugin without uninstalling it." arguments: - name: "<plugin>" description: "Plugin name or `plugin-name@marketplace-name`" required: true options: - flags: "-s, --scope <scope>" description: "Scope to disable: `user`, `project`, or `local`" default: "user" valid_values: "user, project, local" - flags: "-h, --help" description: "Display help for command" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "CLI commands reference / plugin disable" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00

synopsis: "claude plugin update <plugin> [options]" description: "Update a plugin to the latest version." arguments: - name: "<plugin>" description: "Plugin name or `plugin-name@marketplace-name`" required: true options: - flags: "-s, --scope <scope>" description: "Scope to update: `user`, `project`, `local`, or `managed`" default: "user" valid_values: "user, project, local, managed" - flags: "-h, --help" description: "Display help for command" caveats: - "The `managed` scope is valid only for `update`, not for `install`/`enable`/`disable`." source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference section: "CLI commands reference / plugin update" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:20:00-04:00
